title: Codes for Quantum Secret Sharing with a Helper
authors: Eric Chitambar, Sarah Hagen, David W. Kribs, Zhao Ma, Mike I. Nelson, Andrew Nemec
abstract: Helper quantum secret sharing is a form of secret sharing defined by its unique access structure. One special fixed party, called the helper, can work together with any other party to fully decode the secret. A blind helper is one who can provide this assistance while not holding any local information about the encoded secret. In this work, we analyze the general structure of QSS helper codes and present new code constructions. We fully characterize the structure of blind helper stabilizer codes and show that for the encoding of a single qubit, recovery is always possible using one-way local operations and classical communication (LOCC) from the helper to the targeted party. Furthermore, we demonstrate how such codes also allow for the helper to target larger subsets of parties by one-way LOCC, enabling them to be authorized to recover the secret. Finally, when each party only holds a qubit, we identify the general form of all helper codes (including non-stabilizer codes) and find that LOCC recovery is only possible in special cases.
summary: This paper provides a deep structural analysis of Quantum Secret Sharing codes featuring a 'helper' party. It characterizes these codes, particularly the 'blind helper' type, by deriving necessary and sufficient conditions based on stabilizer theory. The work proves that for single-qubit secrets, recovery is always achievable using LOCC from the helper, advancing the theory of quantum information security.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the general structure of Quantum Secret Sharing (QSS) codes, specifically focusing on the unique constraints imposed by the 'helper' access structure.
main_result: It fully characterizes blind helper stabilizer codes for single qubits, showing that recovery is always possible via one-way LOCC from the helper to the target party.
method: The analysis employs stabilizer formalism, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions for helper codes, and comparing structural constraints derived from information theory and quantum error correction principles.
model_or_system: The model is pure QSS schemes where a secret is encoded into a subspace of a multipartite system. The focus is on stabilizer codes, which are defined by commuting Pauli operators on the shared qubits.
key_observables: The possibility of recovery via Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC), and the structure of the logical operators supporting the secret.
important_parameters: The number of parties ($n$), the size of the secret ($k=1$ qubit), and the structure of the access set $\Gamma$.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on pure QSS schemes using isometric encoding, and initial results are derived for stabilizer codes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the recovery of maximal entanglement using information from an authorized subset of parties.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining helper codes, reviewing error correction conditions, characterizing stabilizer codes using structural lemmas (e.g., Lemma 2 for blind helper codes), and finally deriving the general form of qubit helper codes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of information access structures (like helper codes) is fundamental to quantum cryptography and secure quantum computation protocols.
